comparator.sourceNotes: The programme-specific Appendix I 2026–2027, printed pages 55–59 and cohort 9A201-2026, supplies the ordinary English full-time Tilburg sequence: 60 EC in each of three years. Every named course is represented separately; the third-year 30-EC mobility/minor window remains genuine open space. Old Testament: Torah and Prophetic Literature (U20074-B-6) carries 6 EC in the formal cohort table, correcting the general webpage's 3-EC display; there is no missing three-credit unit. Research and academic skills (12 EC) are embedded in named course weights and are not additional credit. Yellow-coded compulsory units rotate every two years and appear once in the specified cohort sequence. Ordinary Hebrew, Greek and Latin requirements are retained; Greek exemptions and replacement of Latin for an intended teacher-training master require the stated conditions/Board permission and are alternatives, not extra components. The merged registry target covers English Tilburg and Dutch Utrecht delivery plus part-time pacing. English full-time is an ordinary representative delivery, not an English-only target inferred from its translated name. The public reader was recorded as published on 14 September 2026; its general body retains a stale 2025–2026 effective-date clause, so the explicitly dated 2026 cohort appendix controls this reconstruction. Appendix and external allocation checked 2026-10-08; the original UCR assessment dated 2026-09-29 is retained without independent reassessment.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target combines ordinary English Tilburg and Dutch Utrecht deliveries and full-/part-time modes. The ordinary English full-time Tilburg delivery provides an explicitly dated September 2026 cohort sequence for the same broad Theology bachelor, without selecting a shortened prior-degree pathway or the optional canonical-degree package. Translation of the registry display name does not establish an exclusive English target; delivery choice is independent of UCR fit.

exception.reason: The programme's defining academic identity is Catholic theology and theology-specific method: biblical Hebrew, Greek and Latin; Old and New Testament exegesis; fundamental and systematic theology; dogmatics; spirituality; practical theology; liturgy and sacraments; church history; canon law; Judaism; Catholic ethics; patristics; and an independent Theology thesis. Only the 30-ECTS mobility/minor window is broadly open. UCR offers adjacent philosophy, ethics, history, sociology, politics, law, literature and cultural analysis, but no sustained theology, scripture, source-language, liturgical or pastoral curriculum. Constructing a 24-course UCR programme from those neighbouring fields would remove the target's defining theological sequence and misrepresent it as a substantive match.
exception.curriculumContext: The formal September 2026 cohort appendix establishes a complete 180-EC ordinary Theology pathway: 60 EC in year one, 60 EC in year two, and year three comprising the 30-EC mobility/minor window, 21 EC of named taught requirements and a 9-EC bachelor thesis. The Torah and Prophetic Literature course is 6 EC, resolving the webpage discrepancy without inventing an extra methods course or padding a semester. Embedded skills are counted within course weights. The selected ordinary language sequence and rotating compulsory courses follow the explicit cohort schedule; conditional replacements and the optional canonical-degree package are not stacked. English Tilburg is one representative delivery of the merged target, alongside Dutch Utrecht and different pacing.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook course rows, including course names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. GOSPHIL111, GOSPHIL212, GOSPHIL214, GOSPHIL311 and GOSPHIL313 support philosophy, ethics, mind, emotion, agency and the self; GOSHIST111, GOSHIST211 and GOSHIST312 support historical inquiry; GOSSOCI111, GOSSOCI214 and GOSSOCI311 support social analysis; MCCLITR112 and MCCLITR211 encounter literary and mythic traditions; GOSLAWJ111 and GOSLAWJ213 touch law, rights and constitutional treatment of religion-adjacent issues. None is a dedicated course in Catholic or systematic theology, biblical Hebrew/Greek/Latin, scriptural exegesis, dogmatics, spirituality, practical theology, liturgy, sacraments, canon law, patristics or theological research. Isolated adjacent humanities and social-science courses cannot support a defensible 24-course Theology progression.
